title: Bore op: clear a hole wider than one ring by walking rings (or a spiral) out to the wall, instead of refusing it

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while fixing #1556 (decision in `docs/decisions/1556-bore-core-door.md`).

#1556 made the Bore op refuse, by name, any hole wider than `3 x tool diameter + 2 x stock to leave`: its ride is a centre dive, one radial sweep and one ring on the wall, and past that size the dive's disc and the ring's band no longer meet, leaving a core. Detect holes now leaves such holes out of a Bore op with a note.

Enhancement: let the Bore op clear a wider hole itself - concentric rings stepping out from the dive at a stepover under one tool diameter (or an Archimedean spiral), each level ending on the wall ring - so a user boring a Ø20 hole with a 6 mm tool does not have to switch to a pocket op. Detect holes would then stop filtering (or filter only past a stated limit).

Notes for whoever takes it: the cut-level ladder and the cutter-centre disk certificate in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore.rs` already carry several passes per level; the links between rings must certify inside that disk. The floor-coverage law test in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_core_tests.rs` (`every_bore_the_ride_takes_clears_its_whole_floor`) should be extended to the wider holes. Engagement of a full-width ring per level is the machining question (stepover choice, maybe a helix entry instead of the centre plunge).

Done means: a Bore op on a hole wider than 3 tool diameters clears its whole floor (pinned by the coverage law over a range of ratios), verify passes it, and the 3d refusal is lifted or moved to the new limit.
